author: blu
body: THE WHOLE CHAPTER IS PURE, and that is a statement about the builtins rather than about the code. `cpu-read-cr0`, `cpu-read-cr3` and the four `cpu-cpuid-*` carry no effect row: they read processor state and change nothing, so reading them is an ordinary function call and every report below can be built during rendering rather than cached. That is the opposite of the disk inspector, where every read costs 512 bytes of heap that is never returned.

author: blu
body: THE FEATURE TABLE NAMES ONLY BITS WORTH NAMING. A full decode of every defined CPUID bit is hundreds of rows that go stale as vendors add more, and an inspector that renamed or mis-numbered one would be worse than no inspector. What is here is the set this project's own code depends on or asks about: long mode and NX because the boot path requires them, the SSE family because the vector types lower to it, RDRAND because the identity code wants entropy, and HYPERVISOR because it answers "am I under codex-vm" in one bit.

author: blu
body: A word for an empty set, because an empty feature line reads as a decode that failed rather than as a register that is genuinely zero. This is not hypothetical: leaf 1 ECX reads zero under codex-vm, so the line for it is empty on the machine this is most often run on, and a reader would reasonably suspect the inspector before suspecting the host.

author: blu
body: Leaf 1 EDX is the original feature word and holds the things the compiler assumes rather than checks: SSE2 is where the vector types land, and TSC is what the profiler reads.
